correctness.rationale: Independently derive the filtered telegraph stationary Beta law f(u)∝(1−u²)^{b−1}; Brownian noise convolves with Gaussian variance B. For z=1/(2B), H=I1/I0 and h=2zH−1, integration by parts yields ∂_z h=(1−b)/z>0 at every root. h→−1 as z→0 and h∼(1−b)/z>0 as z→∞, so all roots cross upward, forcing a unique root; covariance ∂_b H=Cov(t,log(1−t))<0 implies strictly ordered B_*(b). Gaussian total positivity/variation diminution restricts derivative sign changes, converting central curvature into global mode counts; quartic moment identity gives p^(4)(0)/p(0)=−2(1−b)/B_*² and local analytic expansion gives m²=3(B_*−B)+o(B_*−B) and contrast coefficient 3(1−b)/(4B_*²). Independent Gauss–Jacobi moments verified B*(.25)=.53856358,B*(.5)=.31646434,B*(.75)=.18327382 and m²/(B*−B)≈2.996–2.997 near threshold. Finite numerics are corroboration only; zero-crossing and variation-diminishing lemmas supply the universal proof.

final_claim: In harmonic two-state run-and-tumble motion with strictly positive Brownian diffusivity, the known zero-curvature transition condition has one critical thermal variance B_*(b) for each 0<b<1, strictly decreasing from 1 to 0, with globally one/two modes on either side; exact fourth derivative and universal sqrt(3) peak-opening and height-contrast amplitudes hold. For b≥1 the stationary law is strictly unimodal.
limitations: Only symmetric fixed two-state RTP harmonic trap with independent D>0 Brownian forcing, not other potentials, asymmetry or multiple particles.
Asymptotic modal expansions local in B near B*(b), not global uniform error bounds.
